summary: The video presents a landscape photographer’s workflow for a long-lens mountain scene, focusing on post-processing decisions to reveal dramatic atmosphere and peak detail. It opens with aggressive color and mood testing (saturation, contrast, dehaze, split toning) and quickly moves into atmospheric manipulation by borrowing and repositioning clouds, adding texture, and rebalancing light. The practitioner then demonstrates light-building techniques in Camera Raw, followed by edge reduction with dark blur to direct the viewer’s eye toward the peak. A major portion showcases perspective-changing tools (Perspective Warp and Puppet Warp) to reshape peaks and nearby clouds, including a Cerro Torre reference, illustrating how multi-layer atmosphere can be engineered for impact. The session concludes with refined color grading (split-toning, half-color), diffusion, and noise-management steps, interwoven with reflective notes on long-lens strategy, composition, and the role of atmosphere at multiple levels in creating a compelling Sierra Nevada image.

sections.title: Initial color grading and atmosphere shaping
sections.description: Opening segment tests aggressive color reduction followed by selective saturation, contrast tweaks, and early split-toning/dehaze experiments to establish overall mood.

sections.title: Cloud relocation and atmosphere painting
sections.description: Borrowing and moving sky textures, then painting additional texture to blend with surroundings; clouds are repositioned to frame peaks.

sections.title: Light build and tonal balancing in Camera Raw
sections.description: Multiple Camera Raw passes to brighten and warm the scene, with curve-driven adjustments and de-haze to shape light on the mountain and clouds.

sections.title: Dark blur and edge control
sections.description: Applying dark blur to mute peripheral edges, sharpening attention on the peak and exploring diffusion techniques to control local contrast.

sections.title: Perspective Warp, Puppet Warp, and peak sculpting
sections.description: Prominent demonstration of Warp tools to reshape peaks and surrounding clouds; includes constructing Cerro Torre as a demonstration of dramatic peak creation and layering atmosphere.

sections.title: Final color grading, noise management, and editorial notes
sections.description: Final polish with split-toning and diffusion; balancing noise reduction with warmth and color direction, and closing reflections on long-lens processing strategy and multi-layer atmosphere.
